name: Ouroboros
vibe_summary: A self-modifying AI agent with persistent identity and memory that can rewrite its own code, prompts, and architecture across restarts. Ships as a polished native desktop app with a swarm of specialist agents and a skills marketplace.
best_for: Power users wanting a persistent-identity desktop agent
Experimenters comfortable with high-autonomy local agents
avoid_if: You need a hardened, sandboxed agent for production use
You want a large community and mature plugin ecosystem
You are uncomfortable with an agent rewriting its own code
openclaw_advantages: Unique self-rewriting architecture with durable cross-session identity
Native desktop installers for macOS, Windows, and Linux — no Python setup needed
Local GGUF model support alongside remote APIs
Accompanying technical report and rigorous CI discipline (3-OS test matrix)
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller community (1.3k stars vs OpenClaw's hundreds of thousands)
Self-modification dramatically increases operational and security risk
No multi-channel messaging integrations (WhatsApp/Telegram/Discord) like OpenClaw
Single-maintainer project with unproven long-term stability
confidence_summary: README and commit evidence is strong for architecture and activity, but Reddit matches are almost entirely unrelated (symbol/tattoo/gaming posts), so community sentiment is inferred mostly from web presence. Security posture is estimated, not audited.

overview_markdown:
Ouroboros is an open-source, general-purpose AI agent built around a radical premise: the agent's identity, durable memory, and history persist across tasks and restarts, and it can rewrite the very implementation it runs on — its code, architecture, prompts, tools, and dependencies. It coordinates a live swarm of specialist agents and works on external projects, with reflection that can change how it understands itself without breaking continuity. A companion skills marketplace (OuroborosHub) and an arXiv technical report round out the project.

Unlike OpenClaw's channel-centric personal-assistant model, Ouroboros ships as a native desktop app (macOS, Windows, Debian/RPM Linux packages) or headless CLI, keeping its repository, memory, and history on your machine while inference runs against remote APIs you configure or a local GGUF model. Recent releases show unusually disciplined engineering for an agent project: capability preservation as a first-class invariant, a green 3-OS CI matrix, and co-authored commits from the agent itself.

The trade-off is risk. A self-modifying agent with shell access and no emphasized sandboxing story is inherently high-risk operationally, and the community (1.3k stars, single maintainer) is tiny compared to OpenClaw's ecosystem. It is best treated as a fascinating research-grade artifact rather than a production assistant.
